_meta_itemized.notes: Douglas Clyde, County Council, 2020 POST-ELECTION - and A SOURCE PROPERTY THE BRIEF DOES NOT LIST: this filing is the SAME PHYSICAL SHEET as his Pre-Election filing 11860, resubmitted. Every handwritten stroke matches - the candidate block, the four slashed zeros, '277 38' in the Last Report and Cumulative expenditure cells, '-277 38' across all three balance cells, the same signature - and the ONLY difference on the page is the date line: the original '10/25/20' has been STRUCK THROUGH with a single horizontal pen stroke and '12/1/20' written below it with the filer's initial. Under the clerk-correction precedent (a handwritten correction over a struck typed or written value governs) the operative date of this document is 12/1/20; the struck 10/25/20 is recorded here verbatim as what the page also shows. So Summit's corpus carries two document_ids, two DocumentCenter URLs and two cycle labels for what is materially one re-dated cover, and a future de-duplication pass should treat the PAIR, not either sheet, as the unit - though nothing is merged here, because both are genuine county publications and the honest record is that each exists. Consequences for the wave: (1) the pair carries NO period-vs-cumulative conflict to resolve - Current Report is zero on both money rows on both sheets, so the whole of the reported campaign is the 277.38 carried in Last Report/Cumulative; (2) the 277.38 in expenditures is UNITEMIZED ANYWHERE in the 2020 corpus for this candidate, because neither sheet has a schedule; (3) THE ZERO-GLYPH RULING is what makes the contribution row readable at all - four hand-drawn slashed zeros with a stroke through them, affirmative written zeros and not empty or dashed cells, already published as 0 by the cover tranche with the glyph preserved. A negative campaign balance sustained across all three columns is itself a source property: the candidate spent his own money and never recorded a reimbursing contribution. The party line is struck through in pen on both sheets.
